product_scope: Recommended product promise: photo recognition is an assisted logging shortcut that proposes visible foods and a portion range; the user confirms recipe/brand/serving before nutrition is saved. It is not a medical measurement or allergy guarantee.
supported_platforms: iOS and Android with a shared backend contract and platform-specific local inference adapters.
pricing: MVP should budget a local prefilter for every photo plus cloud calls only for ambiguous/complex cases. Candidate cloud list-price anchors: Passio $99/$599/$2,999 monthly tiers with token refills; LogMeal credit-based; Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite $0.25/M input and $1.50/M output; OpenAI GPT-5.4 mini $0.75/M input and $4.50/M output. Actual spend depends on image resolution, outputs, retries, retention, and vendor contract.
popularity_signal: The architecture follows common public patterns: MFP/YAZIO/Cal AI expose photo -> candidate -> user correction, while HealthifyMe publicly describes local food/non-food filtering plus server processing and Lose It historically documented an on-device quantized model.
recognition_behavior: 1) local quality/food gate; 2) local detector/classifier/segmenter; 3) return candidates and confidence; 4) route ambiguous/recipe-level cases to Passio/LogMeal or a generic multimodal API; 5) resolve confirmed items against a versioned nutrition database; 6) display assumptions/ranges; 7) persist corrections as training/evaluation events without raw-photo retention by default.
identified_services: Shortlist: Passio or LogMeal for food-specific recognition plus nutrition grounding; Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite or OpenAI GPT-5.4 mini as a flexible fallback; USDA FoodData Central/Open Food Facts or a licensed regional database for deterministic nutrition records. Provider selection requires a written contract and benchmark.
model_or_provider_confidence: The architecture is evidence-backed but the best vendor depends on SuperNutrition's cuisines, target countries, privacy requirements, and measured correction rate. Do not infer app-vendor contracts from public marketing alone.
local_inference_evidence: Local first-pass is recommended for privacy, latency, offline feedback, and cost control; cloud is retained for long-tail dishes and richer reasoning. Apple Foundation Models/Gemini Nano are optional platform fallbacks, not universal backends.
portion_and_nutrition_method: Ask for reference object/depth/second image or serving input where possible. Return ranges and an explicit assumption list for grams/calories; map the confirmed item to a canonical database record and preserve source/version/unit conversion.
artifact_source: Evidence sources are listed in the app, service, static-analysis, model, and accuracy result files. Key public sources: MFP FAQ, Passio pricing/SDK docs, YAZIO privacy/help, Lose It Google case study, HealthifyMe policy, LogMeal pricing, Gemma 3n, Apple Foundation Models, ONNX Runtime Mobile.
static_findings: Four public XAPK inventories showed no obvious embedded food VLM model; this supports an explicit cloud/hybrid hypothesis but is not proof. Build observability in SuperNutrition rather than relying on reverse engineering of other apps.
reverse_engineering_limits: Third-party app analysis has legal/terms constraints and cannot reveal private backend contracts. For SuperNutrition, use authorized vendor tests, contract review, and own telemetry instead.
candidate_models: Phase 1 local: compact food detector/classifier/segmenter. Phase 2: SmolVLM-256M/500M cross-platform baseline, Gemma 3n E2B high-end Android, Apple Foundation Models eligible iOS, Gemini Nano supported Android. Keep Qwen2.5-VL-3B and current Moondream 3.x as research benchmarks, not initial production defaults.
mobile_runtime_support: iOS: Core ML/Vision plus optional Foundation Models. Android: LiteRT/MediaPipe vision tasks plus optional Gemini Nano/LiteRT-LM. Shared fallback: ONNX Runtime Mobile. Use ExecuTorch if PyTorch export/backends are already strategic.
device_requirements: Define tiers: broad tier with small classifier; high-end tier with local VLM; cloud fallback for unsupported/low-memory devices. Gate by measured RAM/latency/thermal/battery, not model parameter count alone.
expected_food_inference_quality: Success criterion is reduced time-to-log and acceptable corrected nutrition error, not perfect first-pass calories. Enforce abstention for low confidence, mixed/hidden recipes, allergens, and portion ambiguity.
unit_cost_estimate: Track cost per submitted photo, cost per accepted meal, retries, and cloud fallback rate. A local gate that halves cloud calls may matter more than choosing between two sub-cent generic VLM calls. Use vendor-provided usage reports for final pricing.
privacy_and_compliance: Default to no raw-photo retention, strip EXIF, encrypt transport/storage, disclose cloud transfer before upload, provide regional routing/consent/deletion/export, sign DPAs, prohibit vendor training on user photos unless explicitly opted in, and avoid medical/allergy guarantees.
recommendation: Build a two-week spike: (a) local quality gate + compact classifier; (b) Passio and LogMeal integrations behind one interface; (c) one Gemini/OpenAI fallback; (d) 300-500 weighed-meal benchmark; (e) UX for confirmation/ranges. Select the production path only after comparing corrected-item accuracy, calorie/gram error, latency, privacy, and cost per accepted meal.
